findings.title: Null SHA normalization ambiguous in _detect_mixed_sha_checks
findings.body: Original str(x or y or '') expression had unclear intent for non-string/None values. Replaced with explicit isinstance guard: raw_sha = ...; sha = (raw_sha or '').strip() if isinstance(raw_sha, str) else ''. Behavioral impact: none (original was safe, fix makes intent explicit).

findings.title: _proof() STALE/MISSING boundary with proof_path set but no sha
findings.body: Expert suggested empty sha + present path should be MISSING. Re-analysis: STALE is correct — a path without SHA means we know a proof exists but cannot verify currency. This is a conservative staleness signal, not absence. Code is correct as written.

findings.title: Missing explicit null headSha/head_sha test cases
findings.body: Added test_explicit_null_headSha_not_treated_as_mismatch, test_explicit_null_head_sha_rest_field_not_treated_as_mismatch, and test_head_sha_rest_field_stale_blocks. Test count: 28 → 31, all passing.

findings.title: head_sha REST field not unit-tested for mismatch detection
findings.body: Added test_head_sha_rest_field_stale_blocks confirming REST head_sha field triggers MIXED_SHA_ARTIFACT_SET blocker when stale.

commit.message: fix(pr-steward): fail closed on mixed-sha artifact sets

remaining_risks: mypy not run — type annotations present but not statically checked
Mixed-SHA detection reads check.headSha (GraphQL) and check.head_sha (REST) fields; a third field name used by future GitHub API responses would silently bypass detection
MISSING substate requires both proof_path and proof_head_sha to be absent/empty; a harvest with only proof_path set (no sha) classifies as STALE, which is conservative but worth noting

schemas/pr_steward/pr_state_snapshot.schema.json was also updated (required to accept proof_freshness); this schema is not validated by the test_intake.py fixture tests but is validated inline via validate_artifacts()
